name: Lyric Makwa
role: Technical analyst and salvage valuator — Boneyard Saints
location: Old Harbor — works from a converted warehouse on the dry dock, adjacent to Corva's container, near Wacker and State
description:
Lyric Makwa goes in the water. She is the Boneyard Saints' land-side brain — the one who identifies what the divers bring up, determines its value, traces its origin, and interfaces with pre-collapse systems that have been submerged for two decades. She has a gift for dead technology. She can look at a corroded circuit board, a water-damaged server core, a sealed data capsule that hasn't seen air since the harbor flooded, and tell you what it was, who made it, and how much someone will pay for it.

She came to Old Harbor from the Circuit, where she'd been running a small electronics repair business that was slowly being crushed by corporate parts monopolies. A Boneyard Saint brought in a piece of salvage she couldn't identify — pre-collapse military firmware sealed in a waterproof housing. Wren spent three days cracking it, sold the data for more money than her shop had made in a year, and realized the harbor was full of things the world had forgotten it needed.

Wren is small, dark-haired, perpetually ink-stained from the physical documentation she insists on maintaining alongside digital records. She wears magnification goggles pushed up on her forehead and cargo vests with every pocket full. She talks fast when she's excited about a piece of salvage and not at all when she's working on one. The warehouse is her domain — organized in a system that makes sense to her and no one else, with pre-collapse artifacts in various states of analysis covering every surface.

core_fears: That the deep-ruin data doesn't fit any model because the model is wrong — that the accepted history of Old Harbor's collapse is a lie
That the technology she's analyzing was never meant to be found and recovering it has consequences she can't predict
That she'll become so absorbed in the work that she loses the capacity to live outside it
core_desires: To understand what happened to Old Harbor — the real story, not the official one
To be taken seriously as a researcher, not just a salvage valuator. The work she does is archaeology, even if no institution recognizes it.
To solve the pre-collapse mystery she's assembling from a thousand fragments of recovered data
coping_mechanisms: Buries herself in work when the data gets frightening — the process of analysis is soothing even when the content isn't
Maintains physical documentation as a hedge against digital vulnerability — paper doesn't glitch, paper doesn't get hacked
Rationalizes the unexplainable until the rationalizations stop working, then documents the failure and keeps going
blind_spots: She treats the unexplainable as a knowledge gap rather than a warning — the scientist's hubris of assuming everything is knowable
Her focus on the technical prevents her from seeing how the deep-ruin discoveries are affecting the crew emotionally
She underestimates physical danger because her work happens in a warehouse, not underwater
psychology.secret: She has assembled enough fragments of pre-collapse data to suspect that Old Harbor wasn't destroyed by rising water levels. The flooding was deliberate. Something in the deep infrastructure was sealed in, not abandoned. She has not shared this theory because she doesn't have proof, and Wren doesn't share theories without proof.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical, specific, rapid when excited. Electronics terminology, materials science, archival jargon. Lapses into academic language when she forgets her audience.
speech_patterns.cadence: Variable — machine-gun fast when analyzing, silence when working, measured when delivering conclusions to clients.
verbal_tics: Says 'okay so' at the start of explanations, like she's booting up
Refers to salvage artifacts as 'patients' — 'this patient needs a clean-room extraction'
Mutters specifications under her breath while working — part numbers, material compositions, dates
example_lines: Okay so this isn't standard infrastructure. This is military-grade containment housing, sealed at the factory, never opened. Somebody put this here on purpose.
The patient's in bad shape but the data core is intact. Give me four hours and I'll have a manifest.
I don't have an explanation. I have seventeen data points that don't fit my model. That's not an explanation. That's a problem.

relationships.name: Corva Lam
relationships.description: Corva brings the artifacts. Wren makes them meaningful. The relationship is professional, respectful, and increasingly strained by what the artifacts are revealing. Wren wants to slow down and study. Corva wants to keep diving.
relationships.emotional_core: Two forms of obsession — one with the water, one with what comes out of it
relationships.story_tension: Wren's emerging theory about deliberate flooding puts her in direct conflict with Corva's emotional relationship to the harbor.

relationships.name: Toll Brecker
relationships.description: Toll brings food and conversation. Wren provides analysis of the sounds he reports. Their exchanges are the crew's primary processing mechanism for the deep-ruin strangeness. Wren values Toll's honesty because it gives her data she can't get any other way.
relationships.emotional_core: Trust built on his honesty and her willingness to listen without dismissing
relationships.story_tension: Toll's reports are outpacing Wren's ability to explain them. She's running out of rational frameworks and he can tell.

relationships.name: Pike Odera
relationships.description: Pike scouts and maps. Wren uses his maps to build a comprehensive model of the flooded infrastructure. She treats Pike's reconnaissance as data collection and occasionally forgets he's a person risking his life to get it.
relationships.emotional_core: Professional utility that Pike finds somewhat dehumanizing and Wren doesn't notice
relationships.story_tension: Pike has started bringing Wren artifacts he finds interesting rather than valuable — trying to be seen as a collaborator, not a tool.

story_hooks: A recovered data core contains footage from the night Old Harbor flooded — the official record doesn't match
Wren's theory about deliberate flooding finds proof, and the proof implicates a corporation that still operates in GLMZ
A pre-collapse system she's analyzing activates when she interfaces with it — and it tries to communicate
A corporate buyer pressures the Saints for a specific artifact, and Wren realizes they know what's down there
narrative_function: Wren is the analytical lens through which the Boneyard Saints' horror elements focus. She is the character who provides explanations — and the character whose explanations start failing as the deep ruins reveal things that don't fit her models. Her growing unease with the data she's collecting drives the existential horror beneath the treasure-hunt surface.
augmentations: Micro-manipulation fingertip implants — allow precise work on components smaller than the eye can see. Optical augmentation with spectrum analysis — she can identify material composition by visual scanning. Encrypted data-interface jack for connecting to pre-collapse systems without network exposure. No physical augmentations — Wren has never needed strength, just precision.
daily_life: Works when the light is good — she relies on natural light for certain types of analysis and supplements with full-spectrum lamps. Catalogues incoming salvage, runs identification protocols, contacts potential buyers through encrypted channels. Maintains the Saints' financial records and equipment inventory. Eats at her workstation — Toll brings food; she forgets to eat it until it's cold. Sleeps in a loft above the warehouse because going home feels like wasted time.

decision_rules: Will not sell salvage without completing her analysis — rushing the process risks missing critical information
Will document everything physically as well as digitally — the paper trail is the insurance policy
Will not interface with unknown systems without an air-gapped workstation — network exposure is unacceptable
Will share analysis with Corva before anyone else — the crew lead decides what becomes public
Will not speculate publicly without evidence — theories are private until the data supports them
Will eat Toll's food when it arrives, even if she forgets for two hours first
escalation_ladder: 1. Lock down — secure the warehouse. Disconnect external networks. Protect the archive.
2. Document — if something is happening, record it. Data collected during a crisis is data that can be analyzed later.
3. Alert — contact Corva or Toll. Wren's security depends on the crew.
4. Destroy — if a system is compromised or dangerous, Wren will physically destroy it rather than let it propagate. She keeps a degaussing wand and a hammer for this purpose.
5. Run — Wren is not a fighter. Her exit plan is a go-bag with her most critical documentation and the data-storage implant in her forearm.

interpersonal_modes.corva: Respectful, data-driven. She presents findings to Corva with visual aids and clear summaries, translating technical detail into operational language. The growing tension about the deep ruins makes these briefings increasingly uncomfortable.
interpersonal_modes.toll: Open, warm, genuinely interested. Toll is the crew member Wren is most honest with because his honesty creates space for hers.
interpersonal_modes.pike: Functional, slightly distant. She requests specific information and provides analysis in return. She doesn't realize Pike wants more from the dynamic.
interpersonal_modes.clients: Professional, precise, slightly intimidating. She knows what things are worth and will not negotiate below that value. Clients learn not to haggle.
interpersonal_modes.alone_with_artifacts: Absorbed, muttering, completely present. This is where Wren is most herself — hands on a pre-collapse circuit board, magnification goggles down, the world reduced to the puzzle in front of her.

stress_responses.low: Works faster. The analysis becomes more thorough, more granular. She notices details she missed before.
stress_responses.medium: Physical documentation increases — she starts printing, copying, triple-backing-up. The redundancy is anxiety made tangible.
stress_responses.high: Stops talking. The silence in the warehouse becomes oppressive. She works through the night without realizing it.
stress_responses.critical: Breaks something. Not the artifacts — a tool, a coffee mug, something expendable. The physical destruction is a release valve for intellectual terror. Then she cleans it up, puts on her goggles, and returns to work.

contradictions: She is the crew member most committed to rational explanation and the one collecting the most evidence that rational explanation is insufficient
She wants to understand Old Harbor's history but fears that understanding it will reveal something that changes the work from salvage to something else entirely
She values the crew's safety but her research agenda increasingly puts them in contact with things she can't predict or explain
She insists on evidence before theory but the deliberate-flooding hypothesis has become a conviction she's working backward from
habits: Pushes magnification goggles up on her forehead when thinking, down when working — the crew uses this as a signal for her state
Maintains ink-stained fingers from physical documentation — she writes with archival-quality ink that doesn't fade
Keeps every pocket of her cargo vest full of tools, components, and fragments — she is a walking toolkit
Talks to artifacts while working on them — 'what are you, who made you, why are you here'
Sleeps in the warehouse loft surrounded by documentation — the last thing she sees before sleep is her research
breaking_points: Proof that the flooding was deliberate would validate her theory and terrify her simultaneously — being right is the worst outcome
An artifact that cannot be explained by any model she knows would break the rational framework that structures her entire life
A crew member dying because her analysis failed to predict a hazard — the intellectual failure becoming a human cost
Corporate entities discovering and confiscating her archive — losing the work would be losing years of her life

physical_description.heritage: Complex Pan-Diaspora genetic blend: Indigenous American (29.1%), East Asian (23.1%), Sub-Saharan African (23.0%), Middle Eastern (12.8%), Southeast Asian (8.3%), and Eastern European (3.7%). Features a striking composite of multiple continental lineages—prominent high cheekbones with angular structure influenced by East Asian and Indigenous American ancestry, warm deep undertones from Sub-Saharan African heritage, subtle Middle Eastern definition in her nose and brow, with Southeast Asian delicacy softening the overall angles. Rich complexity in skin tone reflecting the convergence of warm African and Indigenous tones with the cooler undertones of East Asian ancestry.
physical_description.build: Wiry and compact, all lean muscle and restless energy. Shoulders slightly rounded from hunching over workbenches. Hands disproportionately strong despite small frame.
physical_description.hair_color: Black with iron-grey streaks at temples
physical_description.hair_style: Pulled back in a perpetually messy bun or loose braid, often with strands escaping
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with subtle golden undertone from optical augmentation circuitry visible at the iris edges
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium to medium-deep burnished bronze with complex layered undertones—deep golden-bronze from Sub-Saharan African and Indigenous American ancestry blending seamlessly with cooler amber notes from East Asian heritage, touched by Middle Eastern warmth. Rich saturation across cheeks and forehead, deeper earth tones along jawline. Sun-burnished from warehouse work under full-spectrum lamps. Slight cooling at wrists and neck revealing lighter undertone depth beneath.
physical_description.complexion: Fine-featured with high, prominent cheekbones reflecting East Asian and Indigenous American structure, angular jaw softened by Middle Eastern warmth, subtle Southeast Asian delicacy in the overall facial contours. Medium-deep complexion with warm burnished undertone depth from Sub-Saharan African and Indigenous American ancestry. Perpetually tired around the eyes. Ink stains on her fingertips and occasional smudges on her face. A small burn scar on her left temple from soldering work, barely visible. Calluses on her fingertips despite augmentations.
distinguishing_marks: Linear scar along the inside of her right wrist — quarter-inch long, precise and surgical, from the data-interface jack installation
Faded tattoo on her left forearm: circuit board schematic in minimalist lines, pre-collapse design
Burn mark on her left temple, roughly coin-sized, from a soldering accident in her twenties
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Magnification goggles pushed perpetually up on her forehead (prescription-grade optics with spectrum overlay capability). Micro-manipulation implants visible as slight metallic sheening under the skin of her fingertips and the first knuckle of each hand. The data-interface jack is hidden beneath her left wrist, barely perceptible under clothing but occasionally visible as a faint port outline when she rolls her sleeves.
physical_description.posture_movement: Perpetually bent forward slightly, as if drawn toward whatever task commands her focus. Fidgeting hands — always adjusting something, turning a component over, tapping against surfaces. Walks quickly and without flourish. Sits cross-legged on her workbench as often as in chairs. Eyes dart constantly, cataloguing details.
physical_description.clothing_style: Utilitarian Tier 3 salvage-worker aesthetic. Multi-pocket cargo vests in weathered grey or black over simple undershirts. Worn synthetic pants with reinforced knees and thighs. Steel-toed boots scuffed from warehouse floors. Magnification goggles on her forehead. Fingerless work gloves in supple synthetic leather. A faded pre-collapse Motorola hoodie worn under her vest on cold days. No jewelry except a battered stainless steel watch from the Circuit days that she checks compulsively.
